language: Dart (Flutter) for the app; TypeScript (NestJS) for backend
build_system: Flutter SDK 3.16+, standard `flutter build web`. No special quirks.
test_framework: flutter_test (no existing screen-level tests in the project)
verification_instructions: 1. Run `cd web_app && flutter analyze` — must produce zero errors. 2. Run `flutter build web` — must complete without errors. 3. Manually verify the /connections route in a browser.
environment_constraints: Windows workspace. All Flutter commands run from the web_app directory. The backend is deployed at https://campuscore-bfrq.onrender.com/api/v1 — no local backend needed for building/analyzing.
contribution_requirements: Run `flutter analyze` before committing. Follow existing patterns: ConsumerWidget, FutureProvider.autoDispose, AppColors constants, Nunito font family, no hardcoded strings, no hardcoded hex values.
key_patterns: 1. Screens extend ConsumerWidget or ConsumerStatefulWidget. 2. Providers are FutureProvider.autoDispose at file scope; actions (POST/PATCH/DELETE) are performed inside ConsumerStatefulWidget methods using ref.read(apiClientProvider). 3. AppBar uses AppColors.navyDark. 4. Error states use a local _ErrorWidget with retry callback. 5. Loading states use skeleton widgets. 6. withValues(alpha:) replaces deprecated withOpacity(). 7. Responsive helpers: Responsive.isMobile(context), getPaddingEdgeInsets, getSpacing, getGridColumns. 8. Imports always use relative paths (../../../).
directory_structure: web_app/lib/ contains: app/ (router, shell, theme), core/ (constants, network, providers, storage, utils), presentation/screens/<feature>/ (one dart file per screen). New screen goes in presentation/screens/connections/connections_screen.dart.
